name: FormalMATH
abstract: FormalMATH is a large-scale Lean4 benchmark of 5,560 formally verified statements, from Olympiad challenges to undergraduate theorems across algebra, calculus, number theory, and discrete mathematics. The strongest prover reaches 16.46% under practical sampling budgets — formal reasoning remains largely open.
contributions: 5,560 formally verified Lean4 problems — over twenty times the scale of MiniF2F's test split.
A human-in-the-loop autoformalization pipeline: specialist LLMs draft statements, multi-LLM semantic checks and negation-based disproof filter them, and IMO-medalist-level experts verify.
Reveals pronounced domain bias: provers do far better in algebra than calculus, and over-rely on simplified automation tactics.
method: Statements are autoformalized from natural-language problems, then filtered by semantic verification and disproof of negations.
Provers are evaluated under fixed sampling budgets; a proof must check in Lean4.
The paper also finds natural-language solution guidance can hurt formal proof success.

metrics.name: Success rate
metrics.note: Share of statements formally proven within the sampling budget (pass@32 for whole-proof generation).

leaderboard_note: Scores are from the FormalMATH technical report under its stated sampling budgets; settings differ by prover family.
